implementation.api: createObservedDynamicPlasmaUserSendReadAdapter(options) returns frozen quote(input), createWorkRequest(input, originalPlan), assemble(input, originalPlan, suppliedMaterial), validateUnsigned(input, originalPlan, accountBlock).
implementation.options: Exactly {transports, accountExchange}. The existing request-bound collector captures the two distinct frozen DP callRead capabilities. Only the existing closed account wire is constructed over the caller-provided exchange; no endpoint/host/native connection owner is constructed.
implementation.input: Exactly8 ordinary descriptor DATA fields: observedUserSendReadVersion:1, phase:UNSIGNED, paymentRequired, accepted, payerAddress, compiledSporkIds, policy, runtimeContextDigest. No caller account result, observation, subject, acknowledgement or operation capability can be added.
implementation.capture: One bounded descriptor-only snapshot spans initial input, original plan and supplied material/block before any callback. Existing selected-intent request/profile/payer/spork checks run before reads; original subject rebinds to the selected intent for later stages.
implementation.sequence: One explicit operation: account-before -> existing request-bound dual DP collection -> account-after -> captured existing observed DATA adapter stage. Both account reads use the same selected payer and the existing closed account grammar/ID/envelope path. Non-active/incoherent DP data refuses before the second account read.
implementation.accountGate: Require matching projected address/chain/height/hash around the DP reads. Later stages also require that projection to describe the ORIGINAL subject's previous hash/next height before any DP handoff. The after-read text goes into the existing DATA adapter, which independently decodes/rechecks it again.
implementation.originalPlan: Existing initial subject/quote/ack plan and all later work/assembly/complete key-work-hash-price return contracts stay unchanged. No quote/pair/ack refresh, block repair, payment replacement or re-signing is implemented.
implementation.busyAndHold: One operation at a time; busy precedes hostile/reentrant input inspection. Any failure after the first account handoff permanently holds that instance without further handoffs. No reset, fallback or automatic retry. Pre-read input refusal does not consume a cycle. Invalid quote/material/block semantics can still consume reads before the existing final stage refuses and holds.
implementation.readBudget: The same captured account wire admits32 explicit handoffs, hence at most16 complete two-account-read cycles and fewer if failures consume handoffs. Existing DP wire/collector budgets remain unchanged. Exhaustion does not recreate a transport or reset IDs. These bounds concern this composition's handoffs, not arbitrary effects of injected capabilities.
implementation.promiseBoundary: Reuse the captured core's prehandled account Promise, safe native reaction settlement and owned internal Promise constructor shields. Never assimilate an external thenable or inspect rejection reasons. Existing unsafe-Promise prehandling obligation remains with the exchange/transport owner.
implementation.projectionBoundary: Equal projected reads are not atomicity/isolation, authentication, ancestry, simultaneous/current state, full previous-block/hash/signature/confirmation proof or protection from ABA/unobserved changes. Coherent supplied raw data can be forged.
implementation.operationalBoundary: Injected callbacks remain caller-owned capabilities, not sandboxed/read-only guarantees. Their owner retains endpoint identity, deadlines/cancellation, unsafe rejection prehandling and terminal native cleanup. No timer, close/cancel capability, real endpoint or lifetime guarantee is added.
implementation.authorityBoundary: This instance's volatile busy/hold state is not durable custody, restart recovery, consumed payment authority or signing-state proof. Creating another instance grants no permission to refresh originals, reset consumed authority or replace/re-sign a payment.
implementation.noEffects: No SDK/current-account-state preparation, real PREPARE, work/nonce search, key generation, signing, publication, payment, SQL/store qualification, provider setup/READY or active buyer cutover. Planner stub, locked SDK105 and real signer stay unchanged.

positiveScope: Factory construction invokes no exchanges and captures options/capabilities despite later option/array mutation. Four existing unsigned stages complete via exactly account-before, six reads on each DP endpoint and account-after in the fixed synthetic fixture.
The same initial plan/block/ack survives fresh declared p=10 prices at +1/+2 Momentum; +3 refuses and holds without further reads. No repricing or original acknowledgement refresh occurs.

Changed/foreign bracket projections refuse; an advanced original account refuses before DP at every later stage. Unavailable/malformed/wrong-ID/empty account results and unavailable/incoherent DP data hold without retry/fallback.
Selected input, original plan, public/nonce material and existing block are captured before an account callback can mutate caller DATA; input objects are neither frozen nor rewritten.

Pre-read exact version/phase/arity/plan/descriptor/proxy/sparse-array/prototype refusals invoke no input hooks or reads. An owned pending account read and reentrant DP callback keep the busy gate ahead of hostile input inspection.

Safe failures drain; decorated Promises, external thenables and controlled inherited constructor/species drift refuse without hook invocation. The test exchange prehandles rejection before deliberately unsafe mechanics.

Signed/damaged/replacement block DATA refuses without repair and holds. Unchecked unprojected previous-block fields and reproducible DATA outputs demonstrate explicit non-authentication/non-authority limits.

Sixteen explicit quote calls on the SAME instance consume account IDs1..32 and96 reads per DP fixture endpoint; the next call and subsequent held call add no exchange handoffs, transport recreation or ID reset.
Captured DATA stage functions remain in use even when their public prototype methods are patched after module load.
